newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel turned lower against the dollar on Thursday after two days of sharp rises, as the market continued to seek direction, dealers said.
"The market was very quiet and volume low. After two stormy weeks the market is looking for direction," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.

The Israeli shekel rose 2.4 percent against the dollar in the three previous sessions after tumbling five percent in the last week of June. The shekel began falling after the government instituted changes in the exchange rate mechanism and the Bank of Israel slashed interest rates 1.2 percentage points June 18.
"Activity was at the lowest level we have seen in the last few weeks and one big transaction can move the whole market in either direction," the dealer said.
He added that the market remains very nervous. "Spreads are still high at 100 points reflecting investors' uncertainty."

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.5170 shekels against 3.5050 on Wednesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.8131 against 3.7980 on Wednesday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 3.0767 shekels per 100 yen compared with 3.0625 on Wednesday, and against the mark at 2.0053 shekels compared with 2.0030 on Wednesday.
In late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.5190 shekels.
- Dan Gerstenfeld, Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211 x233
